_comment: Validate-mode golden: design §6's unmarked-private-data nudge,
over hand-written IR (no Clang needed, so this runs on every lane).
`optional` is the positive: it marks `value_` `\expos` and leaves
`engaged_` -- state of the same kind, in the same class -- unmarked.
That inconsistency is the signal, not the bare absence of a mark: see
check_private_data (validate.cpp) for why the rule is narrower than
§6's literal text; a measurement over the corpus headers is the
evidence that decided it.
Four negative controls, which must stay silent:
- `widget` has unmarked private data (`data_`) and marks nothing
`\expos` at all -- the shape ten of the fifteen corpus headers
have, where the member is filler no wording names. This is the
control the literal reading of §6 would report.
- `optional`'s `hard_reset` is an unmarked private *function* in the
very class that trips the nudge; §6 omits it silently.
- `optional`'s `size_` is private data that is nonetheless described,
so the reader can see it and there is nothing to nudge about.
- `handle` marks its only data member `\expos`, leaving no unmarked
data behind -- a class that got it right.
Every finding here is a Note, so `--validate` exits 0 and still renders;
EXPECT_EXIT 0 pins that, as it does for validate_noexcept_throws.
`kind` is a field on each roster entry: `function` (the default, so
an entry omitting the key reports nothing) or `data`. It is a separate
axis from `disposition`, which is why it is a separate key.
